key_insight: CareMirror reframes dementia care by making caregiver wellbeing a first-class part of the care ecosystem, not an afterthought. It connects caregiver reflection, personalized support, and selective sharing with clinicians to better support families over time.
problem_solved: Family caregivers of people living with dementia often carry heavy emotional and practical burdens, but their own wellbeing is rarely tracked or supported within standard dementia care workflows.
method: Designed CareMirror as an interconnected caregiver- and clinician-facing wellbeing ecosystem.
Used the system as a design probe in semi-structured interviews with 14 caregivers to study longitudinal reflection, personalized support, and caregiver-controlled clinical sharing.
Collected caregiver feedback to inform how wellbeing tools can fit into real dementia care routines and relationships.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper highlights the importance of human-centered, longitudinal systems that support vulnerable stakeholders beyond the primary patient. It also shows how AI-enabled tools can be designed for trust, control, and collaboration in healthcare settings.
visual_elements: Two-panel ecosystem diagram showing caregiver app and clinician dashboard with data-sharing flow.
Journey timeline of caregiver wellbeing over time with reflection checkpoints and support moments.
Icon set for emotional burden, practical tasks, personalized recommendations, and consent-based sharing.
Simple workflow chart illustrating caregiver input -> insight generation -> optional clinician visibility.
paper_title: CareMirror: Bringing Caregiver Wellbeing into the Dementia Care Ecosystem
paper_authors: Jiayue Melissa Shi, Ethan Nguyen, Drishti Goel, Upasana Natarajan, Shashwat Srivatsa
